newsitem.title: UK: NatWest shares fall as sale hopes subside.
newsitem.headline: NatWest shares fall as sale hopes subside.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc fell on Friday after the company announced a shake-up of its investment banking arm, disappointing those who were anticipating NatWest Markets would be sold off, dealers said.
The shares fell 8p to 858-1/2p having earlier traded as high as 877p.

"The point is that people were looking for NatWest Markets to be sold off and the rest of the group might then have been bid for by somebody else," said Ian Poulter, banking analyst at Williams de Broe.
"But that is not the way things are shaping up, although the changes made seem sensible."
NatWest had earlier surprised analysts by revealing the details of the reorganisation ahead of its first-half results next week.
The bank said it had appointed Konrad Kruger as the new chief executive of NatWest Markets. Kruger is currently co-chief executive of NatWest Global Debt Markets.
The company said it was also removing the Treasury, Foreign Exchange, Interest Rate Trading, Money Markets and Currency Options functions to put them into a new Global Financial Markets section.
The review of operations came in response to a 90 million stg loss on interest rate options trading.

"This announcement came as a surprise when they only needed to wait until next week to tell us. The fact that they're sorting things out internally doesn't preserve any premium rating on the shares," said one analyst who declined to be named.
